title: The third digest
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The third digest. The laundromat owner has moved the rack six inches closer to the door. Wood notices. She says the flyers were getting wet.

panels.composition: The laundromat. WOOD in the door with a stack. The free rack — moved. Six inches nearer the door. He stops.

image.prompt: a young man in a laundromat doorway holding a stack of booklets, looking at a wire flyer rack set close to the door, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The floor: four small dents in the linoleum where the rack's feet used to be.

image.prompt: close on a linoleum floor with four small dents where a rack's feet once stood, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The LAUNDRY owner folding towels at the table, not looking up.

balloons.text: Then it was the other thing.

image.prompt: a laundromat owner in a cardigan folding towels at a table without looking up, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood setting the third digest in the rack. The rack in the light from the door now. He doesn't say thank you. She doesn't say you're welcome. The dryers.

image.prompt: a young man setting a small booklet into a wire rack lit by daylight from a laundromat's door, dryers turning behind, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Six inches nearer the door. 'Then it was the other thing.'
